messages:
ash: quick RFC follow-up from allocator sync: proposing an orchestration layer to coordinate evict/renew decisions across the runtime so we don't thrash when small keys are churned.

mira: can you sketch what the orchestrator actually does?

ash: short: maintain soft-global view (not strong consensus) of token budgets, per-tenant token counts, and a tiny moving-window of renew qps. Evictors consult the orchestrator before hard-evicting: if orchestrator believes key is likely to be renewed within grace, prefer non-token victims. Aim is to reduce micro-holes and avoid repeated compaction.

ben: how is this different from the lease-broker or hybrid token ideas? seems similar.

ash: overlaps, but focuses on cross-component flow control: broker handles renew batching and per-key state; orchestrator mediates backpressure if renew storms happen, enforcing quotas, circuit-breaker semantics, and preemption rules. Broker + orchestrator = coordinated renew/evict choreography.

mira: important: we mustn't introduce synchronous RPCs on the eviction hotpath. Orchestrator responses must be cacheable and cheap.

ash: agreed. design: orchestrator publishes small delta updates to local runtime caches via pub-sub every ~200ms. Evictor consults local cache with a lock-free read. In rare cache-miss cases evictor falls back to default policy.

ben: what signals does orchestrator use to make decisions? CPU pressure, compactor backlog, renew QPS, tenant token usage, device memcpy queue depth?

ash: yes to all. signal list: node_cpu%, compaction_queue_len, renew_qps, token_budget_util, device_dma_qps, p99_alloc_latency. We'll normalize into a single score per-tenant and a global pressure flag.

ops-bot: ops reminder: when adding node-level signals, coordinate with infra for stable kernel metrics and sample rate.

mira: fairness: if orchestrator throttles renews globally during spikes, dedicated tenants with SLA should have override path. How do we handle that?

ash: plan: orchestrator supports priority classes. Each tenant assigned a class (default, premium, sla). During pressure, use weighted token budgets and allow preemptible tokens (best-effort) for default tenants. SLA tenants get reserved tokens up to their committed quota; breaker trips only after reserved exhausted.

ben: race risk: renew arrives and orchestrator cache says allow, but by time evictor acts the token may be consumed. Need idempotent flows and final arbiter.

ash: final arbiter is the eviction commit: evictor will check a per-slot serial number before freeing. Renew RPC increments serial and writes a marker. Evictor only proceeds if serial unchanged. That keeps evict idempotent without synchronous locking.

mira: performance/bookkeeping cost? incrementing per-slot serial for millions of tiny keys could be heavy.

ash: optimize: only keep serials for leased keys; for others use a bloom-ish recent-renew cache. Most keys won't be leased. Also we can batch serial bumps for groups.

perf-bot: quick scoreboard from prototype run "orch_1": fragmentation -10%, compaction_cycles -20%, renew_qps down 42% after coordinated throttling, evict p95 +3ms under mixed chat+embed workload.

ben: telemetry we need: orchestrator_score_history, token_budget_used_per_tenant, renew_downgrade_count, evict_serial_conflicts, preempt_count, device_dma_batched_bytes.

mira: safety: if orchestrator process crashes, runtime should fall back to conservative policy (evict aggressively) and emit a large alert. Also ensure no single orchestrator instance can become a global hotspot; design for distributed orchestrators with eventual consistency.

ash: rollout: alpha single-node orchestrator co-located on dev clusters, runtime flag off by default; beta multi-node with per-region coordinator for Dedicated; GA tune defaults and expose console knobs for budgets and priority classes.

ops-bot: checklist: arch note, infra knobs for cpu pressure metric, console metrics plumbing, and bench infra booking.

ash: bench plan posted: steady chat streams + 25% spiky tenants + adversarial renewer. Metrics: fragmentation ratio, compaction cycles/sec, p95/p99 alloc/evict latency, renew fail rates, and throughput. I'll post results in 72h.

ben: volunteer to prototype serial bump batching and bloom cache.

mira: i'll prepare a short 1-page arch blurb and coordinate infra.

perf-bot: scheduled bench: `orchestrator_bench --id=orch_9933 --runs=6 --pattern=mixed_spike` on benchpool-3
